Theme

Work & responsibility · Civic life: news, government & the law

apply verb

for a post, a place

also apply for, apply for a job, stand for, run for office, application, applicant, candidate, defeat at the polls, lose an election, run for (an office)

classical

Cic. Att. 1.1.2: nēmō est enim ex iīs quī nunc petunt
Liv. 26.18.7: professus sē petere
Traupman 180

petō, petere, petīvī (petiī), petītum

verb, third conjugation, with an accusative

apply for, seek (a post); stand for (office)

Lewis & Short: “to apply or solicit for an office, to be a candidate for office”: cōnsulātum petere (Cic. Phil. 2.76). The same verb serves for any post or place one asks to be given.

Other words

  • nōmen profitērī — give in one’s name (as a candidate, a volunteer)

    verb phrase; profiteor, second conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Liv. 26.18 (Lewis & Short); Sall. Cat. 18.3 (Lewis & Short)

  • petītiō, petītiōnis f. — application, candidacy

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.1.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • candidātus, candidātī m. — candidate, applicant

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.1.2: firmior candidātus; Traupman 178; Traupman 286

    From the whitened toga (toga candida) of those standing for office.

  • repulsa, repulsae f. — rejection, being turned down

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.280 (Lewis & Short): repulsam ferre; Traupman 179

    Lewis & Short: “the class. technical phrase” for losing an election; see fail.

Examples

  • nēmō est enim ex iīs quī nunc petunt quī, sī in nostrum annum reciderit, firmior candidātus fore videātur

    For of those now standing there is no one who, if his election falls in my year, would look like a stronger candidate.Cic. Att. 1.1.2

  • quattuor et vīgintī fermē annōs nātus, professus sē petere, in superiōre unde cōnspicī posset locō cōnstitit

    About twenty-four years old, he declared that he was standing, and took his place on higher ground where everyone could see him.Liv. 26.18.7

  • Petīsne illud mūnus?

    Are you applying for that job?composed

  • repulsam ferre

    to be defeated, to lose an electionCic. de Or. 2.280 (Lewis & Short s.v. repulsa)

See also position, job, fail.
